title: Functional-group perception rules
description: The substructure queries behind chem::FunctionalGroups. Every flag the pharmacology, ADMET and stability heuristics key on is one SMARTS pattern here, so a group definition can be read, argued with and corrected without a rebuild. The `key` of each entry must name a bool member of chem::FunctionalGroups; an unknown key or a malformed SMARTS is reported by key (chem::groupPackErrors()) rather than silently leaving the flag false, because a flag that is false because its rule failed to parse is indistinguishable from a flag that is honestly false.

groups.label: aromatic ring
groups.note: Any atom perceived aromatic by chem::perceiveAromaticity and lying in an SSSR ring.

groups.label: phenol
groups.note: Hydroxyl on an aromatic carbon. X2H excludes the phenolate (-O with no H) and any ether oxygen.

groups.label: catechol
groups.note: Two hydroxyls on adjacent aromatic carbons - the ortho-dihydroxy motif that is oxidised to an ortho-quinone and O-methylated by COMT. Written on the aromatic bond rather than as a benzene ring so a hydroxylated non-six-membered arene is not missed.

groups.label: ester
groups.note: Acyl carbon bearing a second, substituted oxygen. H0 separates it from the carboxylic acid; the trailing [#6] excludes an anhydride-style or carboxylate oxygen with no carbon on the far side.

groups.label: carboxylic acid
groups.note: Acyl-hydroxyl, protonated or as the carboxylate anion: -COOH and -COO- are the same functional group at two pH values, and the ionisation state of a drawn structure is an artefact of how the SMILES was written, not chemistry. Both are matched so a zwitterion such as L-carnitine is not read as having no acid at all.

groups.label: amide
groups.note: Any nitrogen on an acyl carbon, which is what the hydrolysis and basicity heuristics mean by amide (it covers carbamates, ureas and lactams as well).

groups.label: ketone
groups.note: Carbonyl flanked by two carbons. Having both substituents be carbon rules out the acid, ester and amide cases by valence.

groups.label: aryl ketone
groups.note: Ketone with at least one aromatic substituent - the conjugated chromophore behind the photolysis and thermal penalties.

groups.label: aldehyde
groups.note: Carbonyl carbon carrying exactly one hydrogen and one carbon.

groups.label: ether
groups.note: Divalent aliphatic oxygen bridging two heavy atoms and not part of an ester/carbonate. Uppercase O excludes the aromatic oxygen of furan; the recursive exclusion is what stops every ester also reading as an ether.

groups.label: methylenedioxy
groups.note: Acetal carbon bridging two oxygens, one of them on an arene - the 3,4-methylenedioxy bridge of MDMA/MDA/MDPV, whose CYP2D6 demethylenation is the point of the flag.

groups.label: primary amine
groups.note: Terminal -NH2 that is not an amide nitrogen. Includes an aniline, which is a primary amine even though it is not basic.

groups.label: secondary amine
groups.note: Aliphatic nitrogen with two heavy neighbours and at least one hydrogen, excluding amide nitrogens.

groups.label: tertiary amine
groups.note: Three heavy neighbours and no hydrogen. !$(N=*) is what keeps a nitro group - also three-connected and hydrogen-free - out of the amine classes.

groups.label: basic amine
groups.note: Any sp3 nitrogen that is actually basic: not an amide, not an imine or nitro nitrogen, not a nitrile, not an aniline (whose lone pair is delocalised into the ring, pKa ~4.6 versus ~10.6 for an alkylamine), not a sulfonamide nitrogen (whose N-H is acidic, pKa ~10 as an ACID, and whose conjugate acid pKa is around 0), and not itself aromatic. This is the flag the pH-partition and lysosomal-trapping heuristics key on, so a non-basic nitrogen in it would be a wrong answer, not a conservative one.

groups.label: nitrile
groups.note: Terminal nitrogen triple-bonded to carbon.

groups.label: nitro
groups.note: Both the neutral pentavalent and the charge-separated depiction, because SMILES in the wild uses either.

groups.label: halogen
groups.note: Fluorine, chlorine, bromine or iodine anywhere in the structure.

groups.label: sulfoxide
groups.note: Exactly one sulfur-oxygen double bond; the recursive exclusion is what separates it from the sulfone.

groups.label: sulfone
groups.note: Two sulfur-oxygen double bonds.

groups.label: phenethylamine core
groups.note: Ar-C-C-N: an aromatic ring two aliphatic carbons from a non-amide nitrogen. Substitution on either carbon or on the nitrogen is allowed, so amphetamine, methamphetamine, MDMA, tyramine and serotonin all carry the core; a benzylamine (Ar-C-N, one carbon short) does not.

groups.label: catecholamine
groups.note: A phenethylamine core on a 3,4-dihydroxyphenyl ring - dopamine, noradrenaline, adrenaline, isoprenaline. The catechol has to be on the same ring the ethylamine hangs off; an unrelated catechol elsewhere in the molecule does not make a compound a catecholamine.

groups.label: anilide
groups.note: Nitrogen carrying both an aromatic ring and an acyl group - the acetaminophen/phenacetin motif whose CYP oxidation gives a quinone-imine (NAPQI-type) electrophile.

groups.label: MAO-labile amine
groups.note: A primary or secondary amine on an UNSUBSTITUTED, acyclic alpha methylene of an arylethyl chain: the substrate shape monoamine oxidase actually deaminates. Four look-alikes are excluded by construction. (1) alpha-METHYL amines of the amphetamine type: the alpha carbon is a CH, not a CH2, so [CH2] fails - this is precisely why amphetamine survives first pass and phenethylamine does not. (2) an N-METHYL substituent such as methamphetamine's: a terminal CH3 has three hydrogens, so it cannot be taken for the alpha methylene, and methamphetamine's real alpha carbon is still a CH. (3) RING amines - the piperidine of methylphenidate, the pyrrolidine of MDPV, the tropane of cocaine, the pyrrolidine of nicotine: !R on both the nitrogen and the alpha carbon rejects them. (4) AMIDE nitrogens, which are not amines at all. The trailing [C]c requires the arylethyl chain, so this flag no longer has to be ANDed with phenethylamine at the call site.
